feed.title: CEZ Job Finder Research
feed.subtitle: What studies say about AI and resumes – every claim linked to its source, every source graded by how strong it is.

entry.title: Age discrimination in hiring: when it starts, what helps
entry.summary: US tests find no drop in employer replies at 40; it shows around 50. With age stated, Swedish employers reply less from the early 40s.

entry.title: AI hiring laws in 2026: what employers must tell you
entry.summary: In 2026, New York City and the EU make employers tell you about AI screening; Illinois, Colorado, California and Connecticut follow. Few let you ask why.

entry.title: Do cover letters still matter now that AI writes them?
entry.summary: Often yes – many forms we checked had a letter box, and a 2019–20 test found more callbacks with one. AI-written letters now tell employers less.

entry.title: Does an employment gap on your resume hurt?
entry.summary: Short gaps showed no clear cost in the biggest review; long ones cut replies. A reason line helped in one test, not in another. The bias is the employer’s.

entry.title: Hiring discrimination: what studies show, what helps
entry.summary: Field tests find employers reply less to some names, ages and histories. Bias varies by employer. No resume change has been shown to remove it.

entry.title: Are two-column resumes ATS friendly? A 7-layout PDF test
entry.summary: We read one resume in 7 layouts with 3 free PDF readers, not an employer’s system. Our plain page never broke; spaced-out headings always did.

entry.title: Is AI resume screening biased? What the studies show
entry.summary: AI models judge resumes differently by name, gender, age and disability in tests. The direction changes by model and test. Real-hiring data is scarce.

entry.title: Can employers tell if AI wrote your resume?
entry.summary: Mostly no, in tests – most people can’t spot AI writing. About half of hiring managers say they’d care. What studies show, and what to do.

entry.title: Do ATS reject 75% of resumes? Where the number came from
entry.summary: No study shows ATS reject 75% of resumes. The figure traces to a 2012 sales claim. We counted the screening questions on 143 application forms.

entry.title: Opt out of AI training: ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini
entry.summary: ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot and Gemini can train on personal-plan chats. Where each switch is, and what it doesn’t stop.

entry.title: What makes a good resume? The evidence, rule by rule
entry.summary: Resume rules sorted by evidence. Long gaps cost callbacks; typos lower recruiter ratings. Most format rules are career-guide convention, not tested.
